preconditions.description: Input consists of exactly two lines: the first line is an integer representing the length of the string, and the second line is the string itself.
The integer on the first line matches the length of the string on the second line.

preconditions.expression: all(c in '()?' for c in stdin.splitlines()[1])
preconditions.description: The string on the second line contains only the characters '(', ')', and '?'.
The length of the string is between 1 and 300,000 (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == ':(' or (len(stdout.strip()) == len(stdin.splitlines()[1]) and all(c in '()' for c in stdout.strip()))
postconditions.description: Output is either ':(' (no solution) or a string of the same length as the input, containing only '(' and ')' (a valid solution).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != ':(' or (all(not is_correct_prefix(stdout.strip()[0:l]) for l in range(1, len(stdout.strip()))) and is_correct_parenthesis(stdout.strip()))
postconditions.description: If output is not ':(', then every strict prefix of the output string is not a correct parenthesis sequence, and the entire output string is a correct parenthesis sequence.

invariants.description: A helper function to check if a string is a correct parenthesis sequence (balanced parentheses).
A helper function to check if a string is a correct parenthesis sequence (strict prefix check).
